title: DeBiasMe: De-biasing Human-AI Interactions with Metacognitive AIED (AI in Education) Interventions
venue: Proceedings of Workshop: AI Augmented Reasoning (CHI ’25)
extended_summary:
This position paper addresses a gap in AI literacy and human-AI interaction research: most existing educational tools focus on algorithmic or dataset bias, while giving less attention to human cognitive biases such as anchoring, confirmation bias, and automation bias. The author argues that as generative AI becomes embedded in academic work, students need support not only to use AI effectively but also to critically evaluate how their own reasoning and prompting behaviors can amplify bias.

The paper proposes DeBiasMe, a metacognitive AIED intervention designed around two main design ideas: deliberate friction and bi-directional human-AI collaboration. Deliberate friction introduces intentional pauses and reflective prompts into the workflow, while the bi-directional framework targets both the input stage (prompt formulation) and output stage (interpretation of AI responses). The prototype includes a prompt refinement tool and a bias visualization map that surface possible biases and encourage reflection, explanation, and mitigation.

The population and context are university students using generative AI in academic settings. The paper reports work-in-progress and prior mixed-methods user research with university students that informed the design, but it is not an evaluative outcome study. Its main conclusion is that effective AI literacy tools should go beyond technical competencies and explicitly cultivate metacognitive awareness, bias recognition, and adaptive scaffolding for diverse user engagement patterns.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a position paper/prototype description with no controlled evaluation, no experimental design, and no inferential outcome evidence. It is peer-reviewed workshop material, but it does not meet empirical credibility criteria for K-12 intervention evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: The proposed intervention could plausibly affect learner metacognition and AI use, but the paper reports no measurable impact or effect sizes. Its influence is therefore theoretical and currently unclear rather than demonstrated.

interventions.use_case: Metacognitive AI literacy intervention for university students interacting with generative AI/LLMs, including prompt refinement and post-response bias interpretation to reduce human-AI biases.

finding.finding_summary: The paper argues that the DeBiasMe intervention is designed to improve students’ metacognitive skills, especially awareness of bias, monitoring of reasoning, and critical engagement with AI. In the illustrative prototype and prior mixed-methods user research with university students, the tool was reported to make implicit human and AI biases explicit and actionable, but no quantitative effect sizes were reported.
finding.measure: Metacognitive support needs, bias awareness, critical thinking, and reflective engagement in AI interactions (survey/interview-based formative evaluation)

finding.finding_summary: The paper positions DeBiasMe as a bridge between academic integrity policies and students’ everyday AI use, and argues it could inform policy recommendations for frictional design and AI literacy frameworks. This is a conceptual/position contribution rather than an outcomes study, so no quantitative institutional effect estimates are reported.
finding.measure: Policy and institutional implications for AI literacy, academic integrity, and responsible innovation
